policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere כִּקְסָם and ketiv כקסום differ only in defective vs plene spelling of the same noun קֶסֶם 'divination'; both yield the identical sense. ASV 'as a false divination in their sight' renders that noun and no ASV note is mapped to this unit, so the English cannot distinguish the readings. Base qere fallback carries the projection.
